 ASHEVILLE, N.C. (WLOS) — An unusually cold shot of air will hit western North Carolina this weekend.
 Along with the well-below-normal temperatures, strong winds – which could gust over 30 miles per hour – will push wind chills down into the 10s and 20s.
 Because of this, Friday and Saturday will be Weather Warn Days. Bundle up if you're going to be outside, especially during the mornings when it is coldest.
 More details: FREEZING TEMPERATURES, SNOW AT HIGHER ELEVATIONS COMING TO WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA 
 Snowfall with this wintry blast will favor higher elevations near and along the North Carolina–Tennessee state line. The highest peaks there could see as much as six inches of snow by Saturday morning.
 Most elevations between 3,500 feet and 5,000 feet will see between a dusting and three inches of snow.
 Valleys away from the North Carolina–Tennessee state line aren't expected to see any accumulation, only flurries at times.
